newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard unveils Windows CE palmtops.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard unveils Windows CE palmtops.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said Monday it gave its first public demonstration of new full screen technology in its HP 300LX and HP 320LX palmtop personal computers due to hit the market by late spring.

The new line of HP handheld PCs will run Microsoft Corp's Windows CE system and include a full-width 640 by 240 pixel screen, which the company said allows information to be displayed as it appears on a desktop personal computer.
The company said the new models are the only ones running Windows CE thus far to incluude the full-width screen capability. They will also have a special backlight feature.

Tom Carr, product manager for handheld products at HP, said the two new palmtop personal computers will be introduced to the market in early May and are designed to differentiate themselves with unique features at competitive prices.

The HP 300LX will be priced around $500 and provide the 80 character wide screen HP said was unique to the Windows CE marketplace, while the higher-performance HP 320LX will be outfitted with four megabytes of random access memory (RAM) and a Compact Flash spot for storage for around 40 percent more. The screen size enables users to use regular programs or browse the World Wide Web with Microsoft's Internet Explorer.

Both machines have specially designed keyboards to ease typing, Type II PC card slot for storage or communications devices and the HP 320LX has a backlit display with a special power-down feature to preserve batteries.

The HP 300LX has a high-contrast reflective display and two megabytes of RAM. Both machines can operate with a business or home personal computer to download files off a CD-ROM drive, for example, or to synchronize files with a desktop PC.

Carr noted that the 300 series is HP's fourth generation of handheld personal computers compatible with Microsoft's core operating system -- dating back to the MS-DOS compatible HP 95LX. It has also sold the HP 200LX family, the HP OmniGo 100 and 120 organizers and the HP OmniGo 700LX Communicator Plus, which incorporated Nokia cellular telephony. "We've said we were Number One in the field before Windows CE -- we had 100 percent share (of the handheld PC standard market)," he said. HP has shipped more than 200,000 units.
"It's a whole new opportunity for us with our fourth generation of products."

HP said the market research firm Forrester Research expects worldwide demand for handheld PCs to grow by 40 percent a year, with 40 percent of sales in international markets, primarily in Japan and Europe.
The new HP line will include a variety of fax, electronic mail, wireless communications, storage and personal information management features, the company said.
